source_text: Fragmenta in Matthaeum Mt 1, 16 Καὶ Ἀπολινάριος δὲ τὴν τελευταίαν μόνην ἀποδεχόμενός φησιν· ἡ μὲν τοῦ Ματθαίου γενεαλογία φυσικὴν ἔχει τὴν διαδοχὴν τῶν γεννηθέντων, ἡ δὲ τοῦ Λουκᾶ νομίζεται τῶν ἐπιγραφέντων υἱῶν κατὰ τὸν νόμον τοῖς μὴ γεννήσασιν· οὕτως γὰρ «Ἰωσὴφ ἐπιγράφει τῷ Ἠλὶ» γενόμενον ἐξ < Ἰακώβ , ἀπογόνου> Ἰεχωνίου. οὕτως ἐκ διαφόρων ἀρχῶν ἀρξάμενοι ὁ μὲν Ματθαῖος ἀπὸ τοῦ «Σαλομῶνος», ὁ δὲ Λουκᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ «Ναθὰμ» εἰς τὸν αὐτὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἔρχονται. 2 Mt 1, 16 Φησὶ γοῦν Ἀπολινάριος, ὅτι πατρὶ παῖς ἐπιγράφεται. πατὴρ δὲ αὐτοῦ κατὰ χάριν ὁ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ ἅμα κατὰ σάρκα διὰ τῆς γυναικός. καὶ βέβαιον αὐτῷ τὸ εἶναι πατέρα Χριστοῦ τοῦ ἐκ τῆς ἰδίας αὐτοῦ σαρκὸς γεννηθέντος ἥτις ἐστὶ Μαρία , ὅπου γε καὶ τῷ τεθνεῶτι βέβαιον ἦν τὸ ἴδιον εἶναι αὐτοῦ παιδίον τὸ γεννώμενον ἐκ τῆς γυναικὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ ζῶντος ἀδελφοῦ. εἰ γὰρ ἰσχυρὸν τὸ τοῦ νόμου, πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὸ τῆς χάρι τος. ἦν δὲ καὶ ἡ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἐπαγ γελία πρὸς ἄνδρα, οὐ πρὸς γυναῖκα. οὗτος γὰρ τὸ προηγούμενον ζῷον καὶ θεῷ προσεχέστερον καὶ οὕτως ὁ κατ' εἰκόνα. Κατ' ἀμφοτέρας τὰς γενέσεις τοῦ Χριστοῦ πατὴρ ἀναδείκνυται ὁ Ἰωσήφ , κατά τε χάριν καὶ κατὰ σάρκα· κατὰ χάριν μὲν διὰ τῆς μνηστευθείσης αὐτῷ παρθένου, κατὰ σάρκα δὲ διὰ τὸ ἐκ τῆς αὐτῆς εἶναι φυλῆς τήν τε παρθένον καὶ τὸν Ἰωσήφ . 3 μτ 1, 19 Ἀπολινάριος δὲ τὸ δειγματίσαι καὶ αὐτὸς παραθέμενος τὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Ἰωάννου καὶ Θεοδώρου ἐξήγησιν ἐπήγαγεν. 4 Mt 2, 1®12 Πολλὰ τὰ μαρτυροῦντα ἐξ ἀρχῆς τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν, ἀλλὰ τού των ἁπάντων ἀρχὴ φαίνεται εἶναι ἡ τῶν μάγων ἀπαρχή. αὕτη δὲ καὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἁπάντων ἀπαρχὴ λέγεται εἶναι. καὶ οὐ τοῦτο μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ θεόθεν ὁδηγούμενοι καὶ ὑπὸ ἀστέρος τὰ μέλλοντα γενήσεσθαι ἐδήλωσαν καὶ τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀπορίαν λύσαντες κατακρίτους αὐτοὺς ἀπέδειξαν μὴ πεισθέντας τοῖς σημείοις. 6 Mt 2, 18 Πῶς εἰς τὸν Ἰσραὴλ εἰρημένην τὴν λέξιν εἰς τοὺς παῖδας μετήγαγεν ὁ εὐαγγελιστής; ὅτι ἐν τύπῳ τοῦ λαοῦ τὰ βρέφη τὰ σφαγέντα ὑπὸ Ἡρώδου παρείληπται. ἡ δὲ Ῥαχὴλ ὡς μήτηρ τοῦ <πατρὸς τοῦ> Ἐφραὶμ ὑπὸ τοῦ προφήτου μνημο νεύεται. ἔστι δὲ μήτηρ καὶ τοῦ Βενιαμίν, οὗ μέρους τοῦ κατὰ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ ἡ λεγομένη Ῥάμα . ὥσπερ οὖν τοῖς βρέφεσιν ἡ ἀνά στασις ἀπόκειται, οὕτω δηλοῦται καθάπερ ἐκ θανάτου σωθησόμενος ὁ λαὸς διὰ τῆς πίστεως. Εἰς τύπον τοῦ λαοῦ τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ τὰ ὑπὸ Ἡρώδου σφαγέντα παιδία παρέλαβεν ὁ εὐαγγελιστὴς ἀνάγων εἰς αὐτὸν τὴν τοῦ προφήτου λέξιν. 9 Mt 3, 17 Τινὲς δέ φασιν τὴν λέγουσαν φωνήν· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἢ ἀγγελικὴν εἶναι ὑπουρήσασαν τῷ προσώπῳ τοῦ πατρὸς ἢ ἑτέραν ἐκ τοῦ παραχρῆμα κατασκευασθεῖσαν. τὸ δὲ ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα ἐν παραθέσει ἑτέρων υἱῶν εἰρῆσθαι οὔτε ἀγαπητῶν γενομένων οὔτε ἀρέσαι σφόδρα δυνηθέντων αὐτῷ· υἱοθεσίας γὰρ ἠξίωντο καὶ οἱ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ. διὰ δὲ τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς μαρτυρίας καὶ τῆς τοῦ πνεύματος καθόδου δείκνυνται τῆς ἁγίας τριάδος αἱ ὑποστάσεις. 10 Mt 4, 11 Ἀπολινάριος ὁ παράφρων τροφάς φησιν ἐκ παραδείσου διηκόνουν αὐτῷ ἵνα ὥσπερ ὁ μὴ ἀποσχόμενος οὗ προσετέτακτο Ἀδὰμ τὴν ἐκεῖ 1 τροφὴν ἀπωλωλέκει, οὕτως ὁ νέος Ἀδὰμ καὶ ὧν μὴ προσετάχθη ἀποσχό μενος καθ' ὑπερβολὴν ἀρετῆς εἰς τὸ ἐξ ἀρχῆς καλὸν ἀποκαταστῇ. 11 Mt 5, 6 Παρὰ τῷ Λουκᾷ μνημονεύονται μακαριζόμενοι ἁπλῶς «οἱ πεινῶν τες », νῦν δὲ ὁ Ματθαῖος διορίζει τοὺς ἑκόντας καὶ διὰ τὸν τοῦ καλοῦ πόθον τῶν κατὰ σάρκα ἡδέων ἀπεχομένους. ὁμοίως οὖν ἀμφοτέρων ἀκουσόμεθα. ὁ τὴν δικαιοσύνην τοῦ θεοῦ ποθήσας εὗρε τὸ ἀληθῶς ὀρεκτόν, οὗ τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν οὐχ ἑνὶ τρόπῳ τῷ κατὰ τὴν ὄρεξιν ἐνεργου μένῳ ἐπλήρωσεν· οὐ γὰρ μόνον ὡς βρῶσιν τὴν τοῦ δικαίου μετουσίαν ἐπόθησεν· ἡμιτελὴς γὰρ ἦν. νῦν δὲ καὶ πότιμον τὸ ἀγαθὸν τοῦτο ἐποίησεν, ἵνα τὸ ἔνθερμόν τε καὶ διακαὲς τῆς ἐπιθυμίας τὸ πάθος τῆς δίψης
english: And Apollinaris is said to accept only the last [genealogy]; for Matthew's genealogy is natural, having the succession of those born, but Luke's is considered to be of the sons inscribed according to the law for those who did not beget; for in this way, it happened that "Joseph is inscribed to Eli" (Mt 1:16), a descendant of Jacob, from Jeconiah. Thus, having started from different origins, Matthew comes from "Solomon" and Luke from "Nathan" to the same Joseph.

For Apollinaris says, indeed, that a boy is inscribed to a father (Mt 1:19). But his father is Joseph by grace, and at the same time by flesh through the woman. And it is certain for him to be the father of Christ, who was born of his own flesh, which is Mary, where even for the deceased it was certain that the child being born of his wife and of the living brother was his own. For if that of the law is strong, much more is that of grace. And the beginning was also an announcement to a man, not to a woman. For he is the preceding living being and closer to God, and thus the one according to the image. In both the generations of Christ, Joseph is shown to be father, both by grace and by flesh; by grace indeed through the virgin betrothed to him, and by flesh indeed because both the virgin and Joseph are of the same tribe.
And Apollinaris, having set forth this example, also applied the explanation of the blessed John and Theodore.

Many testify from the beginning to our salvation, but the beginning of all these seems to be the firstfruits of the Magi. This is also said to be the firstfruits of all the Gentiles. And not this alone, but being guided by God and by a star, they also revealed the things that were to come, and, having solved the perplexity of the Jews, they proved them condemned for not believing the signs.

How did the evangelist bring the word to the children in Matthew 2:18? The infants slaughtered by Herod are taken as a type of the people. Rachel is remembered by the prophet as the mother of Ephraim [and the father of] Benjamin, of whom the part is according to Jerusalem, the so-called Ramah. Just as a resurrection awaits the infants, so it is shown, just as the people shall be saved from death through faith. As a type of the people of Israel, the evangelist received the prophet's word regarding the children slaughtered by Herod.

Regarding Matthew 3:17, some say concerning the saying of the voice: 'This is my beloved Son,' that it was an angelic substitute for the person of the Father, or something else prepared by chance. But the saying 'in whom I am well pleased' was spoken in the context of other sons, who were neither becoming beloved nor being extremely pleasing to him; for those in the law were also worthy of adoption. Yet, through the witness of the Father and the descent of the Spirit, the hypostases of the Holy Trinity are demonstrated.

Apollinaris the heretic says that food from paradise served him so that, just as Adam, who was not commanded, was losing the food there, so the new Adam, from whom nothing was commanded, might restore the original goodness through an excess of virtue in Matthew 4:11.

In Matthew 5:6, the hungry are remembered simply by Luke as 'the hungry,' but now Matthew specifies those who abstain because of the desire for the good, from the delights of the flesh. Thus, we hear similarly from both. He who thirsted for the righteousness of God found the truly desired thing, whose longing he fulfilled not in any way merely by the one acting according to appetite; for he did not only desire the participation of the righteous as food, for it was incomplete. Now, he made this good thing also drinkable, so that the warmth and the clarity of desire might be the passion of thirst.

english: It shall be shown. Such a person is said to be filled. But this fullness is not from a turning away, but it makes an increase of the desire. The heart sees God (Mt 5:8); for the incorporeal seizes the incorporeal. And the heart, having perfected the perfection which it was receiving, thus shall see the perfect thing. This happens to it through the cleansing of those things which hinder, just as the eye, being cleansed from the hindrances of sight, sees the light.

How then does the divine Scripture say, 'No one has ever seen God' and 'No one shall see my face and live' and 'Whom no man has seen, nor is able to see'? (Mt 5:8) How then do you say that 'no one has ever seen God'? We say that He is seen and seized through the Word; or, through the divine Scripture, we see God with the eyes of knowledge, or through the wisdom manifest to all, we see through reasoning the One who made [all things], just as in the case of human creations, the maker of the work in question is seen in a certain way by the intellect. But not the nature of the artisan is seen, but only the technical skill. Thus also, he who sees God in creation does not depict the essence, but the wisdom of the One who made all things is portrayed. Is it not then true that the Lord says God shall be seen by the pure in heart, promising so, and the Scripture does not lie, neither [saying] that anyone has seen God nor [saying] that anyone is able to see?

But he who is removed through righteousness, the present things and the future things, instead of these, will bear fruit, for righteousness is not unjust toward its own (Mt 5:10). For it is necessary to strive to keep the brightness given to us in a high place and not to cover it up through sloth, of which the couch resting the body with fleshly pleasures is a symbol (Mt 5:15); for the beautiful is not to us by nature, but by a gift. But such a thing, being neglected, departs. And the glory of God, placing the end of works before us, leads us away from our own ambition.

A virtuous life is light (Mt 5:16). The law judges fleshly things, those things done through the flesh, but the Lord, sanctifying spirits, requires blessedness through the Spirit (Mt 5:21-22). Therefore, he calls the spiritual one 'brother,' the one dwelling according to the Spirit, being named brother.

Because of this, Paul will be indignant with those who are sinning (Mt 5:22). But if it is not said in vain, as some wish it not to be—for if he sins, he is not spiritual, and the one who is not spiritual is not truly a brother—he hands the murderer over to the judgment of the law, but the one raging is handed over to the eternal judgment. Theodore and Theodore are recorded as saying in vain what was not actually said.

Regarding Matthew 5:22, he says that the one who called his brother 'Raca' is liable to the judgment of the saints. For he who blasphemes against the common part sins. Raca, indeed, calls the despised one, as another says; for so also among the Syrians the scoundrel is called. But what he says regarding the soul rather, he speaks of judgment and testing; for not indeed, if someone says only these things, will he be responsible for the punishment, but he will be much more without responsibility having said other things.

Regarding Matthew 5:29-30, concerning the bodily things he speaks of members; and excessively, not that one must actually cut off the members, but such as to kill them and to set them aside sluggishly for sin, as the Apostle has said; and not to spare even the most necessary things, if through them someone is to experience a bad activity. It is not necessary to cut off the members, but such as to kill these and make them inactive toward sin. Regarding Matthew 5:34, the heaven is therefore the throne of God, since God is holy and 'rests among the saints'; but He is not contained by such a throne, but pervades all things by a creative and watchful and sanctifying power. Regarding Matthew 5:48, the man is perfect in imitation of God in his own measures.

Regarding Matthew 6:1-2, in other matters he speaks of righteousness, thus calling almsgiving. But the aim of almsgiving he sets before us as the glory from God, not from men; for whoever wishes to please someone, he receives praise as a reward from them. Not indeed he who has already been seen has done it for the sake of being seen, but he who wishes to be seen and is doing this also. Regarding Matthew 6:11, give us today the coming and destined food, the life-giving one, and in the present age, as if providing a pledge, providing the Holy Spirit. Regarding Matthew 6:34, if caring for one day is heavy and wretched, how is the excess not unmanageable? If caring for one day is both heavy and burdensome, how much more would caring for many things be wretched and senseless. Regarding Matthew 7:6, the word is holy and a pearl, the heretics are dogs and pigs.

How does the evangelist lift up the word brought to the cross according to Isaiah (Isa 53:5) into healings (Mt 8:17)? Because even his passion was a healing for men, and the Lord suffered no more than he worked through those dishonoring him and through his own death, preparing and fighting against the life of men by setting himself apart for them. Isaiah brought the word to the cross, but Matthew to the healings of diseases; and he did this because even that passion of the Savior was a healing for men, and it is evident that his death also granted life to us.

“You have come,” they say, “before the time of the prophetic words” (Mt 8:29), the demons hearing, because Christ is about to come into the world through the flesh of your flesh and because he is about to judge them in the consummation. “You have come to torment us before the time,” that is, before the consummation.

Why then are they worthy to enter into the swine (Mt 8:31)? When they are not able according to men, they desire according to the irrational, of those things which are through man, just as the misanthropes harm him or his own things. Seeing such a small sign, the Gergesenes entreat Jesus to depart from their borders (Mt 8:34), because they had no desire for the good. For they did not say this judging themselves unworthy, but as being unfeeling and exceedingly unfaithful.
Because they had no desire for the good, but were lazily dividing and sluggishly toward the grasping of the great good.

“An old garment,” he said, [speaks] the old man; “but a coarse cloth” the new Word (Mt 9:16-17), and a joining of these does not happen; immediately the fast and the spiritual joy; for spiritual susceptibility in a bodily man is not. For having been accustomed to seeking the things of the flesh, he will never find joy in these, but the matter will appear harsh and unendurable to him and will be separated from him more, because the thing being dragged along burns him. And the fasts are old and the old men; but new wine is the new Word, which they cannot contain; for their soft [material] is torn, not bearing the strength of the spiritual life. And the Word was not given to such people for what is necessary.

These things, therefore, the Lord says, regarding the renewal of the foremost of the disciples which is about to be at his resurrection, with which it is already the time for spiritual exercises (Mt 9:27-31). No one boasts if the power speaks about itself that it is able; but it would be boasting for one who does not have the power by nature, but receives it by grace to say 'I am able.' And the Savior commanded the blind not to say anything about what happened, teaching us not to show that it is necessary; for it was not boasting toward God to speak the truth about it. And the confession of those who were healed concerning the healing did not bring a charge, but testified to gratitude.

He did not completely cut off those from the Gentiles about to believe, nor the Samaritans, desiring 'all people' (Mt 10:5-6) to be 'saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth,' but it was necessary first to go to 'the lost sheep of the house of Israel,' just as he himself says toward the Canaanite: 'I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel,' which God promised to seek through the prophet Ezekiel. But they lost the law having been given to them, not having guarded it.

And he says 'has come' (Mt 10:7) not as if it were approaching; for it had approached of the incarnate Lord, but as far as those who have not yet believed, it seems Christ is far from them. For I want to show the deacons of the Gospel to be entirely free and prudent, not being humbled by care for any single thing of the body (Mt 10:9-10). And Matthew says both he and Luke [say] 'neither sandals' 'nor' a garment 'nor a staff,' which seems to be the most modest thing to take, 'on the way.' But Mark seems to permit them to take a 'staff' and 'to have put on sandals' in some of the copies. For he says in others that 'he commanded them so that they might carry nothing on the way,' neither a 'staff' nor a 'bag' nor 'bread' nor 'copper into the belt' nor 'having put on sandals.'

english: Having left Joseph in the hands of Egypt, he went out naked. [Mt 10:10] 'Nor sandals.' It is not fitting for an apostle in journeys to carry death, but to walk with life following the one saying, 'I am the way,' and to step out of a holy land wearing nothing; for they are not 'paths of serpent upon rock,' [Mt 10:10] and perhaps not of any other beast.

For as much as you have the Savior lighting your darkness and guarding 'your entrance and your exit,' [Mt 10:10] you have no need of sandals. Where there is no disorder, but gentleness, there is no need for a rod, so as not to frighten in the beginning by means of the rod; for beautiful sheep turn to the shepherd by voice alone, so if you have the staff, do not fear the rod, which Paul holds up against the Corinthians. [Mt 10:10]

Just as the serpent withdraws from those pursuing and hides himself, [Mt 10:16] so also you, withdrawing from those pursuing, will endure the time of the Gospel without pre-empting [it].

He prepares the apostles so as to become ready for the things that will happen and not to be disturbed, [Mt 10:19-22] and at the same time [shows] the power of God helping them and his own proclamation, and neither the madness nor the unbelief of the Jews being spared, nor even of their own. 'And you will be hated,' he says, 'by many'; [Mt 10:22] for this is that which is by all; for many were there receiving them in their houses and loving them. 'And he who endures until the end, this shall be saved,' he says; [Mt 10:22] for he who only having been bold and believing in the beginning, but not until the end, this one is not a partaker of the promised good things; for in every matter, both good and bad, the end is indicative.

english: Now what is being proclaimed is this: it is until the continuous [end]; for 'until' means being sent along with all time up to this point. He says that the kingdom of the heavens comes by force to those to whom it comes, because it is necessary by force to grasp bodily nature and to be held together by spirit, having died to the world but living to God, which thing law and prophets did not yet have (Mt 11:14).

And he says that Elijah is John according to the power and the spirit of Elijah. And since what was being said was unclear, it was left to those capable of understanding the knowledge. This also the angel Gabriel said concerning him: 'and he will go out before him in the spirit and power of Elijah,' showing this one to be so, even if the one seen was a different person (Mt 11:14).

Instead of 'that all things had happened justly'; for from which he repented some, it was being shown not idly nor in vain that the things having happened were fulfilled; for this is the justifying of wisdom, to receive the presence of wisdom as its own, just as children. And wisdom is also justified from works, according to wisdoms being performed, or from words (Mt 11:19).

'And you,' he says, 'Capernaum, resisting the honor and undergoing judgment' (Mt 11:23). Foreseeing the transition of the Word to the nations because of the disobedience of Israel, he praises and glorifies the Father on our behalf, the ones who shall be benefited. And he gives thanks to his Father and to the Lord of heaven and earth, the Lord being in symmetry with the slaves and offering thanks for the things of slaves toward a Master.

And he says, according to the pleasure of the Father, that the mystery concerning him should be hidden from Israel, the wise nation, but be revealed to the foolish nations first. Through which it is shown both that the coming did not fail to encounter God, nor did the presence of Christ fail the intended purpose, but these things happened because God had forewarned and having pre-ordained the [plan] of grace...

The justice of God's good pleasure is kept silent here, but is shown in another way. For the good pleasure of God is not irrational, nor do men attain knowledge and wisdom in any other way than through themselves.

If the yoke is kind and the burden light (Mt 11:30), how did he call it a 'narrow' 'way'? It is narrow for the reckless, for the earnest find the commands of the Lord to be light; for even if there is a little bodily toil, the God-fearing man, now being nourished by good hopes, bears these things.

Having examined the bitter [ones], they demonstrate them to be not philanthropists against those who do no wrong (Mt 12:7). Therefore also he remembers the prophetic word, which prefers showing mercy over sacrifice.
And you, man, if you have a withered hand, having heard from the Savior: stretch out your hand while Jesus is working at good deeds, and it shall be restored to health like the other (Mt 12:13).

Those teaching in the marketplaces do not do this for the sake of benefit, but of pride and also of vainglory. Therefore, they fail in the purpose of teaching and in being slandered by all. Thus the Savior teaches us not by word alone, but also by manner, neither shouting nor making a show and publishing faults; for it is so harmful for us to be disposed in this way, whereas the opposite is both most useful and most profitable.

Again, the power to cast out demons by the Spirit (Mt 12:28) is as much possible for a man to have without being turned aside, according to the economy. If the energy of the Spirit is the kingdom of God, I do not by any means think the Spirit to be an addition to the divinity, being brought in from the servile creation into the construction of the divine kingdom.

english: A man was seen to have come through lowliness and a despised nature. But the judgment interpreted according to the law—neither for this present age nor for the coming one—is not to be forgiven. For when the law commands the condemned God to die, and the Lord is held against the law, [it does] not grant forgiveness for such a thing.

But if the forgiveness through baptism is kept silent in such matters, since there was not even a time to discourse with the Jews about this; for there is found a certain distinction between the [judgment] in this age and the coming one, that the one being baptized will be from this age; and a certain distinction is examined between the present and the coming life, and thus it holds a denial of the examination from the law, according to Paul the speaker saying, 'God is the one who justifies; who is the one who condemns?' (Romans 8:33). Does not the doing of wonders and the loosening of demons, which only the Spirit does, leaving these things to the demon, leave you no forgiveness for the blasphemy? He says this, not refusing that the blasphemy against himself be forgiven, nor [refusing] a place of repentance for those blaspheming against the Spirit, if they wished, but claiming that the blasphemy against him, as against a man, would then only seem to be a lesser thing when compared to the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, but after the resurrection from the dead and the ascent to heaven and it being clearly shown that he is truly the Son of God and God. Even if he has become unchangeably a man, the blasphemy against him will not be forgiven, unless through a sincere repentance of his fault.

From this we learn (Mt 12:43-45) that a demon will not overpower a man of better disposition, but such a one will be an impassable barrier to him, having virtue preceding, and leaving no place for him, as the Preacher advises. On the contrary, the evil and reckless man is a rider for the evil spirit regarding the good. And we learn that the demons also possess a certain consolation for those who are suitable to themselves; for when they are not able to do this, they do not rest, just as it is said from the opposites that the rest of the Divine Spirit is the suitability toward men; for 'the Holy [One] rests in the holy [ones]' (Ps 99:2).

God. But the entering in with many after the one-time departure has a cause in the unchangeable wickedness of man. And the seven spirits are to be considered much; for among the multitudes, many times the seven are [mentioned] according to the divine Scripture. In the beginning, indeed, the evil spirit dwelt among the Jews, when in Egypt they were idolaters; but it departed when they were called by God. After these things, when it had failed against the one who was called, then the grace passed over to the Gentiles, and they were being given out. And the one among the Gentiles became a dwelling of the evil ones, both harsh and inaccessible, having received God, the Gentiles. But the return to Israel is easier than before, and with a great multitude of the exodus. Therefore, it is bad that they now pass through, being constantly arranged toward the blasphemy against Christ as in Egypt, not having the covenant toward Abraham, and not expecting according to justice even as then, but being cut off from hope, because they have rejected the fulfiller of this. Thus the Lord has made manifest in the words toward them both their remaining rejection and the judgment of the coming shame, and the already-established rule by the evil one.

That his brothers did not believe in him (Mt 12:46), we learn from John, and from Mark we have heard somewhat more: as if they were attempting to hold [him] having gone astray. With such a mind, the Lord did not remember [them] as his own, but he demonstrates the subjects; to these he foretells all the names of the relatives, who, according to the intimacy of obedience to him, were joined together. And even if Mary's opposition was only for a time, just as Simeon also foretold saying, 'and your own soul' and the following, it is fitting that the Lord also returned to these things favorably, remembering her passion and having joined her to the beloved disciple.

english: He shows not that it is sown into them, but they themselves. Therefore we say that the Word is both seed and that which received the word through comparison and likeness to himself. Because of this, Christ is formed in us and we are being formed according to Christ.

He likens the world to a sea because of the bitterness and the billows of trouble within it (Mt 13:47), but the power of the Word, casting a net upon the world, gathers from various thoughts of the old and new Scripture, from Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish, men and women, free and slaves, righteous and wicked. The net is filled when the master who casts it knows; for this is not for a man to recognize. When the Word of instruction already has the measure of the fullness, then not all who have undertaken the learning of the Word will be found worthy to the master of the net, but a distinction then will occur between the wicked and the good; and to the useless, the end will appear as destruction, but to the good, the dwelling placed by the Lord into different vessels: for many are the dwellings by the Father. But the wicked, who are counted temporarily with the righteous, will no longer have with them the indistinguishable [state] through weariness, leaving behind for themselves a sweet life, just as fish in the sea; they will undergo the most painful punishment in fire, where nothing remains for the consolation of evil.

The Savior likened the world to the sea because of the trouble and confusion within it, but the power of the Word, casting a net upon the world, was being fulfilled from various thoughts of old and new [Scripture] gathered from every kind of Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish. Of more wonders and greater events by our Savior (Mt 14:17), it is not less that there is not always use of authority for the abundance of food, but it is necessary many times to be in need and to be without (Mt 15:2).
The Lord turns the evil state of the Pharisees into opposites; for those caring for the bodily things despised the spiritual, but the Savior, introducing the spiritual, renounces the bodily.

Indeed, following the preceding demonstration, the voice of the prophet was applied at the right time, possessing much concord with it (Mt 15:8). Where did the Canaanite woman come from? (Mt 15:21-22) From the idolatry of Tyre and Sidon, from her own people, and from 'the house of her father.' Where did she come from? She came forth as a fragrance of myrrh for the Savior; for she holds a type of the Church from among the Gentiles. But also the Savior came out from the 'kinship' of Israel and from 'his own house,' which is Jerusalem. And the Canaanite woman receives him, she who also received Elijah, the widow; and what did she cry out, shouting: 'Lord, Son of David!'? How did she know to call thus, having studied neither the law nor the prophets? She called him 'Lord' according to his divinity, but 'Son of David' according to the flesh. Consider for me the widow's son who was dead, that is, the body which had been made dead, and the soul having been purified from the demon; he restored both the body and the soul.

For neither does a physician satisfy an untimely desire of those who are sick by seeking the remedy of the disease, nor the fulfillment of pleasure; nor does the Savior fulfill an irrational desire in order to show power. For it is not profitable for such people to be showered with graces which, not being sufficient, do not suffice. Moreover, they ask for a sign from heaven, such as foods like those in the days of the fathers, or a standing of the elements like in the days of Joshua. Having said that they are a wicked generation, he leaves the faithful Zion, the synagogue of the Jews, like a bridegroom leaving a city that has become a prostitute. Just as a physician does not give an untimely desire to those who are sick as a way of loosening their disease, nor does he satisfy their pleasure with harmful foods, so also the Savior does not fulfill an irrational desire to show his power; for many signs from heaven they have seen: 'a spirit descending like a dove' (Mt 16:1-4), the heavens having been opened and the paternal 'voice saying: This is my beloved Son.'

Yet he does not provide an apology to those who work the passion through these things; for the mindset and the conspiracy of the Jews did not harmonize with the counsel of God, nor did they hasten then, which God managed; so that for them, what was being done was impiety according to their opinion, but to God it was a wise dispensation and, to mankind, a saving benefit (Mt 16:23).
And that which is in the glory of his Father: he says 'the glory,' meaning the glory of God, because having become man, he is the Son of God (Mt 16:27).

english: As it shows in parallel, having placed both as the Son of Man, saying and that he would appear in the glory of his Father. And he confirms what is being said also with his angels; for the angels are of God, and not of any creature, nor of man. Because of this, indeed, 'Lord of Powers' is a name for God. And a name of identity is a mark of knowledge. And he says that such one appearing gives to each according to his deed.

Regarding Matthew 17:5, the Father announcing the Son appears from the voice heard there, as if proclaiming and itself the testimony coming from above through all; for a voice of God is not to be considered heard [by the ear], nor is the sensible from the incorporeal. And just as 'no one has seen God ever' (John 1:18), neither has [anyone] heard God. But what you hear of his dispensation has the power of necessity; for he says [it is] rather than the prophets introduced by Moses, that the time has already advanced and to depart from the introduction toward perfection, from the types toward the truth; for the law having been introduced through the appearance from above, it was not possible for the greater to prevail among men if not introduced by the appearance from above.

Regarding Matthew 17:22-23, he therefore says that what is going to happen in Jerusalem is not yet approaching, nor the time according to which it was necessary to suffer, so that he might reveal the divine foreknowledge being such, and that he was about to suffer voluntarily, not departing from where he was to be persuaded through ignorance. And it happened for the disciples' benefit so that they would not be troubled as if men had prevailed against him.

Regarding Matthew 17:24, this was a legal matter concerning the drachmas, having been determined by Moses saying: 'each will give a ransom for his own soul, the half of a drachma' (Exodus 30:13). These things indeed the Jews were collecting from everyone, and the drachma was being given as a ransom for two souls according to the law; neither was it being added to the rich one, as the law has said, nor was it being diminished for the poor one 'from the half of a drachma'. That is, he says, the holy [thing] is according to the drachma, nothing else being hinted at regarding the matter, or the true ransom, since all things were being shadowed toward this. And the true ransom was the Lord, having the Father in himself by power, as a divine character is, of which the giving of the drachma is a symbol, even though it is a drachma...

Regarding the redemption, no one can give more than half, even if they become rich. The mystery was that the Son could not be separated from the Father, nor could one understand anything lacking of perfection concerning Christ, whence it is said, 'all the fullness of deity dwells in him bodily' (Col 2:9).

He presents himself as creator and lord of the sea and those in it and every element, as the proper Son of God and Father. For this fish held a type of the church, which of old was seized by the salt and dread of unbelief and was deeply submerged in the depth, and was baptized and tossed by the storm and surge of worldly pleasures; but it was hauled up by the hook of the apostles, through teaching and fishing and the word that hunts, toward the knowledge of God, 'who called us out of darkness into his marvelous light' (1 Pet 2:9).

Because of this, it is fitting to adapt his coming into the world to the previously set parable as if it were a sheep that has become lost; that is, the man being among the hundred sheep, from the multitude of the heavenly powers, being similar to them as a rational being, being counted as a sheep among sheep, yet being the least compared to the great multitude, and therefore one hundred among sheep. But his wandering is the stumbling of Adam. It is sought appropriately that he also remain similar to those remaining with God, and for their replenishment it is necessary, so that the shepherd might not be lacking and be a stump, just as Paul said that they might 'recapitulate all things' in Christ (Eph 1:10), the recovery of the part that had flowed away, since the standing together of the whole in Christ is not complete due to what is missing and lacking.

It is peculiar to the parable to command that the woman and children and all that she has be sold and returned; for regarding human affairs this is possible, but regarding the judgment from Christ, things not owned are not being sold, nor would the repayment of debts occur. english: Having willed to pay the debts of the sins of the world, the Savior has suffered on our behalf. The fellow-servants who also report the one who used the master's servant without restraint are both angels and men entrusted with the administration, such as Paul was, who delivered the most shameful wrongdoer to the devil. And just as the one who has canceled the debt becomes free, so the one who suffered for those against whom he was wronged is set free toward salvation.

One must pay attention even to that, that he was conversing about the necessity of forgiving one another among men, and for this purpose, having used the parable, he began thus: 'For this reason the kingdom of heaven was made like...' (Mt 18:31). For our fellow-servants, not bearing our wickedness, accuse us before God, not as if He were ignorant, but as those indignant against those who strike the laws of philanthropy. And he speaks of angels appointed to the tortures. But 'until he pays all that is owed'—that is, he continuously delivered him over to be tortured—for he was never able to pay; here, indeed, God turns the man toward trials, diseases, and other tortures, but in the future, to be tortured unceasingly for eternity (Mt 18:35). And he did not say 'thus your Father will do to you,' but 'my Father'; for such are unworthy to be named sons of God. Therefore, the word traces in brief the unutterable philanthropy of God, which the one not imitating as much as possible will undergo punishment from the righteous judge. And even if it has been said: 'the gifts of God are unchangeable,' yet wickedness was so powerful as to overturn this word. Thus, the word requires two things of us: to remember a certain one of his own sins and to be unforgetful of kindness toward the one who falls.

The Savior has discussed this in a human manner according to the didactic form, not revealing himself to be the creative Word, nor indeed separating the created Son from the creating Father, but perhaps including the Word in the name of the Father, saying 'all things came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being' (John 1:3). He says that adultery is not living with one's own; but he who abandons his own is not living with his own. Therefore, 'he commits adultery against her'—that is, against the second, whom he joins to the one who is naturally conjoined to him, if he abandons his own. How then does the law not contradict the one saying 'you shall not commit adultery' (Ex 20:14)? We say that the law forbade the manifest adultery when another destroys the one living with him; but the Savior [forbids] even the one not living in agreement with all, nor even known by nature, nor...

english: Being reproved that she is an adulteress, Christ forgives the one who, having committed fornication, departs, because this has dissolved the natural union and it no longer happens by the man. Regarding the division of the Lord, it is possible for those walking in the lower [world] to endure the sorrow in the world rather than to think according to the righteous (Mt 19:10), but for those able to surpass the world, as if being carried by wing-speed toward the upper righteousness, being painless and free from the sorrows in the world.

Therefore, not imposing a yoke, he said: not all grasp the word, but those to whom it is given. And that 'to whom it is given' is a manifestation of natural gifts, which anyone might call a natural aptitude and the intelligence from birth toward the achievement of temperance; for there are indeed some differences by nature toward each virtue, some being more, others less, disposed toward it. Even if natural things are by no means perfect, nor are they unchangeable and entirely unachievable, but even the apt toward good is perfected by practice, and the unapt is healed by much struggle. Not all say they grasp the word, but those to whom it is given. And that 'to whom it is given' is a manifestation of natural gifts and of the intelligence from birth toward the achievement of temperance.

Only evil and corruption of the creation prevents approaching the Creator, but the deficiency of wisdom is not a hindrance to the approach; for he seeks fullness, and by this the approach is granted. Therefore also the precise expression of such things is 'the kingdom of the heavens' (Mt 19:14); for he did not say of these, but of such [as these], since there is also a deficiency of wisdom in children, which the apostle was turning away from saying: 'do not become children in mind, but in wickedness be sober' (1 Cor 14:20). source_text: ὁ θεὸς θέλει ἔχειν τῇ προαιρέσει, τὴν ἁπλότητα, τὴν ἀμνησικακίαν, τὸ ἀγαπᾶν τοὺς γονέας, κἂν τύπτηται ὑπ' αὐτῶν. ἐπετίθη δὲ τὰς χεῖρας τοῖς παιδίοις τῆς ἐπι θέσεως τῶν χειρῶν διδασκούσης τὴν τῆς θείας δυνάμεως ὅπλισιν. 97 Mt 19, 17 Καλὴ ἡ τοῦ νόμου προπαίδεια καὶ οὐκ ἀναιρεῖ ὁ Χριστὸς αὐτήν, ἀλλ' εἰ θέλεις, φησίν, εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν , τήρει τὰς ἐντολὰς ἀρχὴν τῆς ὁδοῦ ταύτης ἐπιδεικνύων, οὐ συμπλήρωσιν· καὶ τὸ μὴ ἀλλό τριον εἶναι ἑαυτοῦ τὸν νόμον διὰ τούτου μαρτυρῶν· ἡ 11 τελειότης δὲ παρ' αὐτοῦ. 98 Mt 19, 23®26 Καλὸν τὸ ἀποστολικὸν ἐνταῦθα ἁρμόζει τὸν «ὄγκον ἀποθέμενοι πάντα »· τὸν γὰρ ὄγκον ἐδήλωσεν ἡ πρὸς κάμηλον ὁμοίωσις· «στενὴ γὰρ καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν ». ἆρ' οὖν καὶ τὰ κακά; ὅπου γὰρ ὁ θεός, εἴρηται, τὸ καλὸν ἕπεται καὶ οὐδ' ἂν ἐννοήσαι τις ὑγιαίνων, ὅτι τὰ κακὰ θεῷ δυνατὰ οὐδὲ ἀδυναμίᾳ εἴποι ἂν τὰ καλὰ μὴ ποιεῖν· ἀσθένεια γὰρ τοὐναντίον ἡ τῶν κακῶν ποίησις καὶ ἀσθενείας τὰς ἁμαρτίας ὁ Παῦλος καλεῖ λέγων· «ἔτι γὰρ ὄντων ἡμῶν ἀσθενῶν κατὰ καιρὸν Χριστὸς ὑπὲρ ἀσεβῶν ἀπέθανεν » καὶ ὁ ψαλμῳδός· ἐπλήσθησάν φησιν «αἱ ἀσθένειαι αὐτῶν »· τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἀσθενείας καλεῖ λέγων. ἀλλ' οὐδ' ἐκεῖνό τις ἂν ἐγκαλέσειεν τῷ λόγῳ τῷ λέγοντι πάντα θεῷ δυνατὰ οἷον λέγειν εἰώθασιν. ἆρ' οὖν καὶ τὸ γένος ποιῆσαι μὴ γεγονέναι θεῷ δυνατόν ἐστιν; ἀχρεῖον γὰρ αὐτῷ πάλιν τὸ τοιοῦτον· οὐδὲν δὲ ἀχρεῖον ἐπὶ θεοῦ δυνάμεως παραλαμβάνεται. ὥστε περισσαὶ πᾶσαι αἱ κατὰ τοῦ λόγου συκοφαντίαι. εἰπὼν δὲ ὁ Μᾶρκος, ὅτι «Ἰησοῦς ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ἠγάπησεν ἀυτὸν » ζήτησιν κινεῖ, πῶς ἠγαπήθη ὁ μὴ μέλλων ἀκολουθεῖν ἐπὶ «τὴν ζωήν ». ἔστι δὲ ἐπὶ μὲν τοῖς προτέροις ἀγάπης ἄξιος ὁ τὰ τοῦ νόμου φυλάξας καὶ ταῦτα ἐκ νεότητος, τῇ δὲ περὶ τὸ τέλειον ὀλιγωρίᾳ τὴν ἐπὶ τοῖς πρόσθεν ἀγάπην τελείαν οὐκ εἴασε γενέσθαι, ὥσπερ οὐδὲ τὴν τελειότητα ἐδείξατο. διόπερ ὁ Παῦλος ἀτελὲς ἅπαν τὸ ἐν νόμῳ κατα λαβὼν ἐπὶ τὴν τελειότητα ἔσπευσεν. 99 Mt 19, 27 Οὐχ ὡς μεγάλα τινὰ καταλελοιπότες, ἀλλ' αὐτῶν, ὧν εἶχον, ἐκ στάντες καὶ τὴν προαίρεσιν ἐπιδείξαντες τὴν ἁπάντων προτιμῶσαν
english: God desires to have through choice simplicity, the forgetfulness of wrongs, and the loving of parents even if they beat him. He placed hands upon the children of the place of the hands, teaching the arming of the divine power.

The early stage of the law is good, and Christ does not annul it; rather, he says, 'if you wish, enter into life' (Mt 19:17), keeping the commandments, showing the beginning of this way, but not fulfilling it; and his law is not something else, testifying through this; but perfection is with him. It is good for the apostolic way here to fit 'laying aside all wealth' (Mt 19:23); for the wealth was shown by the comparison to the camel; 'for narrow and afflicted is the way leading into life' (Mt 19:24). Do the evils then also fit? For where it is said that God follows the good, no healthy person would even conceive that evils are possible for God, or that he would say it is not a weakness to not do good things; for the doing of evils is the opposite of strength, and Paul calls sins weaknesses, saying: 'for while we are still weak, Christ died for the ungodly according to the time' (Rom 5:6), and the Psalmist says: 'their infirmities' (Ps 38:3); he calls sins infirmities. But no one would accuse him by the word that says all things are possible for God, as they are accustomed to say. Is it then possible that the making of the race did not occur for God? For such a thing is useless to him again; and nothing is received as useless before the power of God. Thus all the slanders according to the word are excessive.

Having said, Mark says, that 'Jesus, looking at him, loved him' (Mk 10:21), he stirs up a question: how was he loved who was not going to follow into 'life'? Regarding the former, he who kept the law and these things from youth was worthy of love, but regarding perfection, he did not allow the love upon the following things to become perfect through a lack of time, just as he also did not show perfection. Therefore Paul, having understood all in the law as incomplete, hurried toward perfection. Not as if they were leaving great things, but they, from those which they had, stood up and showed the choice preferring all (Mt 19:27).

english: Christ. According to Matthew 19:28-29, the apostles judge by virtue, reproving evil. And 'now' is the enjoyment of manyfold things according to fellowship, not according to possession; just as the Savior set forth all the things of the brothers for those fighting for the sake of the gospel—thus many houses, and brothers and sisters, and mothers and children, and farms—as an existence for those leaving their own, because love has filled all with kinship and all need.

And Luke also added concerning a woman; and this is according to Paul commanding to honor 'elders' as mothers, and 'younger women' as sisters in all purity. For just as he gives non-brothers as brothers, and non-parents as parents, and non-children as children, so also he gives a non-wife as a wife in another way, namely, manifesting kinship through fullness, not fleshly.

Therefore, to leave behind according to the flesh is a good thing because of the spiritual life, just as Moses said long ago concerning the tribe of Levi: 'He who says to father and mother, I have not seen you, and to his sons, he has kept your words and your covenant and has preserved them. They shall declare your judgments to Jacob and your law to Israel; they shall offer an incense in your anger for all time upon your altar' (Deuteronomy 33:6-8). For there, because of the divine zeal of the race, there is apostasy, and here it is the same; for he does not accept the separation as if God were a stranger, but as if it were not an opportunity to spend time on these things for the one about to be raised up in the ministry of the gospel.

So, therefore, not even the separation from wife and marriage is to be counted as something evil to be praised, but so that even this is not an obstacle to the minister; and the preference of spiritual things altogether shows that the fleshly things are not foreign, unlike the Manichaeans who invalidate the creation of God. And it is no difference to say 'for my sake' or 'for the sake of the gospel' as Mark, or 'for the sake of the kingdom of God' as Luke. For the very name of Christ is the power of the gospel and of the kingdom, and the gospel is hung upon the name of Christ, and the kingdom of God is granted through his name.

english: What the first ones thought—that they would receive more—demonstrates a nature, rather than the intellect of holy men; for they do not reckon this at the time of the resurrection, nor will they accuse then (Mt 20:10). More is owed to the former, because they were living under the rule of death and the devil; for this is the weight of the day and the burning heat, when even the coolness of the Spirit was not present to assist men toward righteousness.

Regarding the cup and baptism, he speaks of death (Mt 20:22); saying 'to drink a cup' as if of wine, just as it is said in Jeremiah that the punishment is to be a 'cup of wine' which one is able to drain and cast down; and 'baptism' signifies the descent into Hades, which had its ascent from there, just as the one being baptized dives into water and rises again; and by saying 'water' he revealed the turbulence of those in Hades.

The event is a sign (Mt 21:2); for it is not a necessity for the one entering Jerusalem with the Lord to sit upon a donkey, who traversed all Judah and Galilee on foot, but to be seen on a colt at that specific time shows the heavenly leader and king sitting upon the new people of Jerusalem; for the colt made the newness of the calling manifest, but also the old, which is not clean according to those now called; for a donkey is not clean according to the law, but is set apart by the various recognitions of uncleanness from clean animals, because the donkey is nocturnal and does not chew the cud.

The people are the untamed colt, upon which neither law nor prophets had seated, awaiting their Lord; for this is also what the Savior said to the sent-off disciples: 'loosening, bring to me' (Mt 21:2). To what, then, was the donkey tied? To the vine, according to what was said: 'binding his colt to the vine and the donkey to the halter.' Loosening, therefore, from the vine, from the first covenant, bring to me.

That [it was done] so that the said thing might be fulfilled: 'The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger' (Ps 32:8). Regarding the times, it did not concern all three evangelists much in the narration of the ascent to Jerusalem; for John, having foretold this more accurately in the first ascent, says that these things were done, and in the third Passover he recounts the passion. Therefore, it only concerned them to recount the event, and they have made [the narrative] into one of the various ascents.

He shows the departure as if from the unworthy; for he comes to take the kingdom away from Jerusalem because of the passion, and [to give] the grace to those migrating to us, just as it was foretold through the prophets, as Jeremiah prophesies: 'I have forsaken my house, I have left my inheritance' (Jer 12:7), and the following. But the fig tree is to be understood here as the synagogue of the Jews and the worship in types and shadows, not having fruit that is edible and pleasing to God, the worship in the Spirit. Therefore, as one not producing sweet fruit, the Lord Jesus dried it up in a certain way, being hungry and seeking fruit from out of humanity. Surely, from what he said, that 'fruit shall by no means come from you' (Mt 21:19), he teaches that the worships according to the law are no longer able to benefit the Jews.

He calls the Householder the God who is the master of all, and the vineyard the people of Israel constructed through piety, saying that he was provided with the security of the help of God, by which, having been delivered from the plot of the strangers, he remained upon his own (Mt 21:33-41).

english: The temple is a tower, in which those approaching were required to offer the fruits of piety to God, all of them fulfilling everything according to the law. Moreover, the altar is a threshing floor upon which the blood of the sacrifices was poured out; the priestly order are farmers, and all those handling this [service], so as to prepare for the people the harvest from the teaching of the law to offer to God with a 'good' 'conscience'.

A prophet speaks of the servants who departed according to the appointed time, those who were sent to make the people or the priests mindful of what is owed to God. For the rebuke was continuous against them, especially against those, more than the rest, who were the causes of the ruin; and they remained enduring all sorts of evils from the Jews, and especially from those who seemed to be in authority among them, without yielding any more. Regarding the Son, he speaks of his arrival (παρουσίαν), having suffered by them and having risen and having destroyed them wickedly (Mt 22:1-14).

This is a wedding of a church being joined to the Word, and a preparation for the wedding through the giving of the gifts of the rich, which is likened to those being prepared for guests in a rich banquet. For Paul says that we are 'in everything' 'made rich' in Christ, 'in word and in knowledge'. The first and second servants are called: the first being those who ran toward the presence of the Lord as fellow-workers and successors of the apostles. But neglect prevents those who are called; for those 'walking according to the flesh' do not follow the divine call toward Christ.

Furthermore, there is the call of the Gentiles, and no longer is there a distinction of race, nor does Israel have the privilege; rather, grace is for those who are negligent and those who are rejected, for 'both the wise and the foolish' as Paul says, and both the evil and the good as the parable says. For he calls those who have taken care of themselves, comparing them to the generally wicked. And the evil may undergo a transition from wickedness, if they entirely obey the good-doing call and 'put on the new man'; but if not this, they were indeed called, but they were not chosen, and indeed their call is overturned; for they are rebuked even for having been convinced of a false entrance. But the ministers who cast out such people are angels. And the binding of feet and hands is...

A cessation of all activity. For no longer is any practice given to the wicked, the time of strangers having been fulfilled in which they have done nothing good. But by saying 'darkness' more externally, he speaks further on of divine virtue and glory.

Regarding the question of those testing [him], as it is recorded (Mt 22:16), witnesses who wished to be present wanted to appear as those most opposed to the true Christ, saying that Christ is of Herod, and as being in authority and able to accuse.

For he did not say again 'I shall not eat it,' but 'I shall not eat,' indicating his sympathy toward the disciples, because he pitied them, as they were going to have the feast unobserved due to his departure; for this is the 'I desired to eat the Passover with you before I suffer,' bringing forth that they shall have sorrow, and he will prefer, over their cheerfulness, that which is profitable to both them and the whole world—not to eat the Passover, but to become himself a Passover, whose fulfillment is 'in the kingdom of God,' when it completely surpasses death; for this is what the word Passover indicates, signifying a surpassing.

english: It was the custom of those eating the Passover, but they were dining. And John has said nothing of a remembrance of the Passover, having made it by saying: 'Before the feast of the Passover, Jesus knowing that his hour had come to pass from this world to the Father, having loved his own who were in the world, loved them unto the end' (John 13:1) and the following. 'Before the feast of the Passover' he says, not in the feast of the Passover, so that we also received 'the first of the unleavened' (Mt 26:11) naturally, having understood [it as] before the unleavened.

It has been said that the good thing is not to have come to execution (Mt 26:24); for non-existence is a preferable state from a bad existence. When Judas went out, John made it manifest; for the servant of the Christ-killing would not have accepted the type of the saving communion; even though the Lord brought him through all other things, but this no longer was permitted.

And for us the type is to expose the wicked regarding the holy communion, even if we bear them through all other things by forbearance; for it is clear that he will kill the Savior, 'he went out' (John 13:27) having been delivered to the devil; for 'after the morsel he entered,' he says, 'into him the Satan' (Mt 26:26), so as having taken him, he led him away as a traitor.

And speaking of many, he says that the blood is being poured out, concerning all, he says that through the one righteous many shall be established (Mt 26:28). This indeed also here shows that one suffers on behalf of many. And Apollinaris makes a type of the participation of the body and blood of that which is being performed in the Spirit for the believers, having imprinted it with the bread as the body and the wine as the blood.

Since the Spirit is the bread of the coming age, which is a food of life for the one approaching the age, and 'the bread which I will give' to you is 'my flesh for the life of the world' (John 6:51), and the blood is living in the body; and for this reason Moses said 'the life of all flesh' (Leviticus 17:11) regarding 'the blood' as being unified by blood. He clearly distinguished the type by the name of the truth, saying: 'this is my body'; and for this reason he named the types with the names of the truth, so that they would not be trivialized by what is seen, but would marvel at the power. Thus, eating and drinking showed the participation which would not have occurred without a body; for if the divine power had not been joined to a body and unified by blood, we would not have had communion through it to God.

Observe that Judas did not die from strangulation, but lived on after being driven [to it] before being suffocated. And the deeds of the apostles declare this, that 'having become rash he struck' (John 13:27) and the following. But this is more clearly recounted by Papia, the pious disciple of John the Apostle, saying: Judas fell upon a great example of impiety in this world; for having become so much a part of the flesh, such that he could not easily pass through the narrowness, it is said that his entrails were spilled out by the narrowness. Having become so much a part of the flesh that he could not pass easily even where the narrowness passes, he could not pass even just the size of the head; for they say the eyelids of the eyes were so swollen that he could not see the light at all, and his eyes could not even be seen by a medical lens; such depth they had from the external appearance. And his genitals, for all shame, were loathsome and greater...

english: It appears that, through him, the discharges and worms dragging from the whole body are carried forth to an excess of only the necessary things. After many tortures and punishments, they say he died in a private place, and because of the stench, this place became a desert and uninhabited until now; but even until today, no one is able to pass through that place unless he stops his nose with his hands.

Judas did not die by strangulation, but lived on after being cast down before being suffocated. And this the acts of the apostles demonstrate, that 'becoming precipitate, he struck the ground, and all his bowels were poured out' (Mt 27:5). This is more clearly recounted by Papias, the disciple of John, saying thus in the fourth explanation of the Lord's words: Judas walked in this world as a great example of impiety. Having become so corrupted in the flesh that he could pass through even where no one passes easily, yet not even the volume of his head [could pass]; for they say the eyelids of his eyes were so diminished that he could not see the light at all, and his eyes could not even be seen by a physician's instruments; such was the depth from the external appearance. His filthiness, indeed, appeared more loathsome and greater than all ugliness, and through it the discharges and worms dragging from the whole body are carried forth to an excess of only the necessary things. After many tortures and punishments, they say he died in a private place, and because of the stench, this place became a desert and uninhabited until now; but even until today, no one is able to pass through that place unless he stops his nose with his hands. Such was his concealment through the flesh, and into the earth.

A good hiding place for those who slander; for those listening were not seeking the truth, and the response was according to the common [custom], which also Luke showed in the history, saying to those asking, 'If you are the Christ, tell us; if I tell you, you will not believe; but if I ask, you will not answer' (Lk 23:8). The scourges [were] instead of the sins of the world, for many are the scourges of the sinner, and according to the prophecy saying, 'I gave my back to scourges' (Isa 50:6). And the righteous has been fulfilled on behalf of the sinners, and the extreme of goodness has been fulfilled, when the 'righteous suffered for the unrighteous' (Isa 53:5), so that 'by his wound we might be healed,' as Isaiah says.

Not because they were strong, but because it seemed to God that these things should happen for the redemption of men, through the dishonoring of the 'Lord of glory' on our behalf, because of the dishonor falling upon us, and the day of the righteous glorifying that which is always being mocked by the uninstructed. english: Because of this, those killing him, not understanding what they were doing, instead performed a symbol: this robe, which is the red garment of Joshua in Jesus, and the one who 'stretched out his hand' being one of the sons of Judah from Tamar, signifies the lifting up of the Savior for the salvation of all, against the blood of the world and the people in it. But those being suffocated by 'cares, wealth, and pleasures,' having taken the word of God and not bringing it to completion, crown Jesus with thorns, insulting him; but he, having taken up our thorns, dissipates them with his own head. And they put a reed in his right hand, supposing it to be his kingship.

The Jews, playing at the Lord as if regarding the name of the prophet, were performing a child's game (Mt 27:28, 30), hence they were saying, 'Prophesy to us, Christ, who is he who struck you'; but the soldiers play at the name of the king; for this is why there is a red robe instead of purple, a crown of thorns instead of gold, a reed instead of a scepter, and the bowing as to a king and saying, 'Hail, King of the Jews.' Upon which was also the spitting and the striking with the reed, which was a task for training soldiers and a thing of a foolish people making a game, just as they have always been accustomed to unfolding the solemn things, being suddenly fulfilled upon the Lord of the prophecy which says: 'I gave you a dream of a fool; I was made mute and did not open my mouth, because you are the one who made me' (Psalm 22:2).

And Phlegon, a philosopher among the Greeks, remembers this darkness as having happened paradoxically on the fourteenth of the moon (Mt 27:45), when no eclipse usually occurs, when the interval from the sun is far, as from the beginning of the heaven to the end; for eclipses happen when these two luminaries approach one another; for a solar eclipse happens by the moon running to meet it, not at the full moon, when it is at the diameter of the moon. This happened as the creation was mourning over what occurred, and therefore making it manifest, that because this opposition was done by the Jews, their mind was darkened and the intelligible sun departed from them. For perhaps they thought him [to be the sun]—for that darkness was raging and a sign of what the hybrids will take in the future; for this happens after all the [acts] of this opposition, when they received a reward from the mockers and did all they wished.

And this is also the beginning of the transfer of souls into the heavens. As many as follow Christ are transferred, as Stephen showed by saying, 'Lord Jesus Christ, receive my spirit' (Acts 7:59), and Paul, 'It is better to depart and be with Christ' (Phil 1:23). The rising of the bodies of the saints made manifest the death of Christ, being the cause of life (Mt 27:52). Not indeed were they shown before the Lord's rising, because first the resurrection of the Savior had to be known, and then those rising through him were to be seen; and it is clear that they rose again for the sake of a sign; for the firstborn of the dead were not being raised to some eternal life, but just like the rest. Luke says that the crowds who came were 'beating their breasts and turning back'; thus even the Jews did not perceive, and in this very passion and dishonor of the Savior, the divine excess was not [perceived], but the usual forgetfulness of men weighed them down and the deception of the teachers brought many. So that it might not be thought that what happened was a fantasy, they were shown to many. And the centurion believed, and those playing and mocking in this way were struck by what happened. Some say also that it is a testimony of this centurion standing firm in the faith after these things.

And indeed they move from their own wickedness, but they serve what is profitable for the matter, not wishing to; for the one who opposes God, through whom [God] opposes, cooperates as those who, through their deed, prepared the foretold glory which they expected to prevent by their deed, having acted against Joseph. The Savior does not forbid worship, but he forbade touch, as John writes; for to be similarly mixed with him was no longer possible before the renewal of men; for it is proper for the new to touch the new.

And Judas indeed betrays Jesus for silver, overlooking the signs he saw, but the soldiers, having received sufficient silver, after seeing [it] immediately reported to the chief priests, beating their breasts terribly, and they spoke of things that did not happen. For the disciples would not have stolen the body, if they had truly been associated with his teaching as to both being dishonored and dying through it, as they themselves reported.

And it does not seem to me to be without purpose that these words were spoken on the mountain of Galilee and not elsewhere; for Galilee is interpreted as the 'overturned' by the Greek language. Therefore also the wheel is called Gelgel. So then, just as these words, having been brought forth from the mouth of the high mountain of salvation, rolled like a wheel against the inhabited world and ran over all, all the nations and cities were baptized into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Mt 28:16-19).
